Purpose We are looking for an experienced Scientist I Medical Device Mechanical Engineer to join our Injectables Device Development team to help us accelerate AbbVie’s combination products from proof-of-concept through submission, industrialization and launch. Our team has end-to-end accountability for commercial development, submission, industrialization and marketed product support for injection devices that enable the delivery of AbbVie’s innovative medicines. In the course of our work, we collaborate with early-stage CMC, Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, Internal and External Manufacturing, and other cross-functional colleagues to ensure timeliness, robustness and market success. As a Scientist I Medical Device Mechanical Engineer at AbbVie you will be part of a multi-disciplinary team of professionals working at the intersection of engineering and biopharmaceuticals. The problems you would help to solve relate not only to the function of innovative injection systems, but also the way in which they interact with drug products and the human body. You would be responsible for advancing programs that combine proven delivery systems with viable commercial drug assets. If you are a self-motivated person who thrives on solving complex problems and are excited by the idea of putting life-changing therapies in the hands of patients, this might be the opportunity for you. Responsibilities Design and execute laboratory studies supporting product development and on-market investigations Support design transfer and industrialization activities Support manufacturing process development activities Maintain product design documentation Support product design changes and continuous improvement effort Perform statistical data analysis Perform 3D and 2D CAD development in PDM environment Develop protocols, and document test results Position required up to 25% of travel time Preferred Qualifications BS in Mechanical or Biomedical Engineering (MS preferred) 3-5 years of experience (MS up to 2 years) ideally in the medical device, drug delivery or other regulated industry Strong communication skills (both written and verbal) Strong design and analytical skills Experience with: Laboratory environment, experiment planning, material control and recordkeeping Physical prototyping (including 3D printing, manual machining, etc.) and reverse engineering 3D CAD modeling, detailed engineering drawings, product database management environment and GD&T Statistical analysis tools Manufacturing processes Design controls (in accordance with ISO 13485 / CFR 820.30) Toolroom environment Knowledge of material properties, material selection and testing methodologies The ability to follow assigned schedules and work in team environment Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent education with typically 5 years of experience, or Master’s Degree or equivalent education with typically two years of experience. Theoretical and practical knowledge to carry out the job functions.

The Toxins group within the Product Development, Science & Technology (PDS&T) - Biologics organization supports manufacturing, process validation, regulatory submission, and continuous improvement for late-stage and commercial manufacturing of biological toxin products at AbbVie. We have an exciting opportunity for a Scientist I position based in Irvine, CA. This role involves leveraging scientific and bioengineering principles to develop bioassays for analytical testing at drug substance and drug product release and stability time points. The candidate must possess in-depth knowledge and hands-on experience in a range of techniques, including but not limited to molecular cloning, mammalian cell culture, PCR, Western blot, protein expression, purification, bioassay, transfection, and laboratory automation platforms. Moreover, excellent communication skills and the ability to thrive in a multi-disciplinary and cross-functional team environment are essential for success in this role. Key responsibilities include: Develop, program, operate, and troubleshoot robotic automation platforms, including Hamilton STAR liquid handlers and Opentrons, to support high-throughput screening and testing. Lead scientific initiatives by generating innovative technical ideas and strategic approaches to advance research goals and address experimental challenges. Demonstrate strong scientific judgment by aligning research activities with project objectives and adapting experimental plans based on new data, evolving priorities, and project developments. Design, execute, and interpret complex experiments using rigorous, reproducible methodologies. Develop, optimize, and implement novel experimental protocols by leveraging emerging technologies to advance scientific progress and resolve technical issues. Maintain current expertise in relevant scientific and technical disciplines and apply best practices from current literature to experimental design, troubleshooting, and method development. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Position Purpose: Performs a variety of semi-skilled, skilled, technical, and administrative work in the planning, scheduling, maintenance of vehicles and equipment within Fleet Services. The Associate Director provides statistical programming support for multiple clinical projects across multiple therapeutic areas, both through individual contribution and through the work of staff. The Associate Director provides training and performance management for staff. The Associate Director demonstrates leadership competencies, builds relationships, and promotes teamwork within the Statistical Programming organization and across functions. The Associate Director is accountable for ensuring statistical programming support is delivered across multiple therapeutic areas. The Associate Director makes key recommendations and decisions related to processes, standards, and resource management. The Associate Director is also responsible for staff management and development. Responsibilities: SAS Programming: Demonstrates a strong understanding of SAS programming concepts and techniques used in the pharmaceutical industry and applies that knowledge to resolve non-routine problems. Standards: Oversees the development and implementation of global company standards for output design and programming conventions and monitors regulatory guidance and industry best practices. CRFs and Database Definitions: Provides strategic guidance on CRF and database design and reviews global standards related to these deliverables. Derivation Programming, Submission Data Sets, and Programs: Interprets statistical analysis plans, develops analysis data set specifications, and oversees the development and implementation of global standards for derived data sets and submission programs. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Works collaboratively with stakeholders to manage priorities and resources across therapeutic areas. Demonstrates a solid understanding of drug development principles, anticipates risks, develops contingency and escalation plans, and contributes to cross-functional initiatives. Communication: Presents statistical programming concepts, risk assessments, and recommendations clearly and persuasively to statisticians, scientists, programmers, and non-scientists. Effectively leads meetings and presentations. Training and Mentoring: Provides guidance, training, and mentoring to staff to support development and ensure compliance with training requirements. Staff Management : Assigns responsibilities, defines scope, and reviews progress to ensure projects are delivered on time and with appropriate quality. Allocates resources to maintain the right balance of expertise across projects and collaborates with management to assess staffing needs. Sets high expectations, promotes open communication, and leads staff to meet organizational goals. Provides performance management for 4–10 statistical programmers. Minimum Qualifications: Degree in Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field 10+ years of statistical programming experience (with MS) OR 12+ years of statistical programming experience (with BS) Strong technical competence in SAS programming and macro development. Experience in pharmaceutical clinical trials. Experience with regulatory filings such as NDA, BLA, or other submissions, including ISS and ISE experience. Preferred Qualifications: Experience interacting with regulatory agencies, especially FDA and EMEA. Previous management experience. Other Required Skills: Working knowledge of ICH guidelines and relevant regulatory requirements. Strong oral and written communication skills.

The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. Broad expertise in analytical techniques, with emphasis on chromatography, compound purification, and spectral analysis. Ability to search scientific literature and evaluate potential solutions to research problems. Effective written and oral communication skills; able to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.

At Visa, AI is central to our vision for the future of payments and commerce. We are committed to building enterprise-scale, responsible AI solutions that deliver measurable value for our clients, partners, and the global economy. The AI Center of Excellence (AI COE), part of the Global Data Office, is at the forefront of this mission—developing reusable AI/ML frameworks, enabling agentic AI workflows, and accelerating innovation across Visa’s data science community. The AI COE operates as both an enterprise capability builder and an AI SWAT team, tackling high-impact projects that address complex business challenges and create scalable, reusable solutions. From evaluating cutting-edge AI methods to deploying reusable frameworks in production, our mission is to improve efficiency, adoption, and business outcomes across Visa’s global Data & AI ecosystem. We are seeking an AI COE Analyst to contribute to technically complex AI initiatives—from research and prototyping through deployment—while advancing reusable AI capabilities and accelerating adoption across Visa. The AI COE Analyst will: Design, develop, and deploy advanced AI/ML methods and agentic AI workflows that address high-value challenges across Visa. Contribute to the creation of reusable AI frameworks, components, and internal open-source assets for enterprise-wide adoption. Evaluate emerging AI/ML techniques, benchmark performance, and validate business impact using real Visa datasets and use cases. Support the end-to-end delivery of AI COE projects, including: Identifying and refining problem statements with stakeholders Prototyping advanced models, pipelines, and automation workflows Building high-quality, reusable code assets Ensuring production readiness and integration with enterprise systems Develop technical documentation, metadata, and best practices for validated AI methods. Contribute to quality assurance through code reviews, prompt engineering support, model evaluation frameworks, and benchmark design. Ensure compliance with governance, security, and Responsible AI standards in all AI COE outputs. Quantify and communicate impact using KPIs such as model accuracy, workflow efficiency gains, adoption metrics, and business value delivered. Collaborate with data scientists, ML engineers, product teams, and global partners to embed AI COE solutions into enterprise workflows and maximize adoption. We have an opening for a NEST Readiness Coordinator to oversee and execute LLNL’s Nuclear Emergency Support Team (NEST) responder readiness program. The position coordinates updates across institutional systems and stakeholders, resolves routine issues by interpreting applicable guidelines, and escalates discrepancies that could impact readiness or on-call coverage. This position will be in the NEST Program Element within the Global Security Principal Directorate’s Nuclear Threat Reduction (N) Program. Partner with the Readiness Program Lead, assess and analyze established readiness support processes and workflows, ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time. The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

About Marvell Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. Your Team, Your Impact We are seeking an experienced Package Reliability Engineer with expertise in 2.5D/3D advanced packaging. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in physics of failure, materials science, and experience working closely with OSATs to drive package reliability improvements. This role requires collaboration with external assembly and test partners, internal design, process, and failure analysis teams, and suppliers to ensure the reliability and manufacturability of cutting-edge semiconductor packages. What You Can Expect Reliability Analysis & Risk Assessment: Conduct physics of failure (PoF)-based reliability modeling for 2.5D/3D advanced packaging. Assess package reliability risks from thermal, mechanical, and electrical stressors. Define and execute stress test plans (e.g., thermal cycling, humidity, electromigration) to validate package robustness. OSAT Management & Collaboration: Work closely with OSAT partners to drive package reliability improvements, process optimizations, and yield enhancements. Define reliability requirements, review test methodologies, and ensure OSAT compliance with JEDEC and industry standards. Monitor and evaluate OSAT performance in executing reliability qualifications and failure analysis. Support supplier audits and technical reviews to assess manufacturing capabilities and reliability processes. Material Characterization & Selection: Evaluate and select materials (substrates, dielectrics, adhesives, underfills) for optimal reliability. Analyze CTE mismatches, warpage, delamination, and interfacial adhesion issues. Work with material suppliers and OSATs to qualify new materials for advanced packaging applications. Failure Analysis & Root Cause Identification: Lead failure mode analysis (FMEA), model-based problem solving (MBPS) and determine root causes of package failures using techniques such as FIB, X-ray, SEM, and TEM. Identify and mitigate interfacial failures, cracking, voiding, electromigration, and stress-induced damage. Drive OSATs and internal teams to implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA). Process & Design Collaboration: Work cross-functionally with internal design, process, and manufacturing teams to define assembly test vehicles and optimize package architectures. Develop and refine design guidelines, process improvements, and reliability best practices. Stay up to date with industry standards (JEDEC, IPC, IEEE, etc.) and implement best practices in package reliability. What We're Looking For Education: Master’s or Ph.D. in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related field. Experience: 5+ years of hands-on experience in 2.5D/3D advanced packaging reliability. Technical Expertise: Deep understanding of physics of failure (PoF) methodologies for package reliability. Strong knowledge of materials science, particularly in interconnects, substrates, and interfaces. Proficiency in stress modeling tools (ANSYS, Abaqus, COMSOL, etc.) for thermo-mechanical analysis. Experience with failure analysis techniques such as C-SAM, X-ray CT, SEM, TEM, FIB, and EBSD. OSAT Collaboration Experience: Proven track record of working with and driving OSAT partners for package reliability, yield, and continuous quality improvements. Experience managing OSAT qualifications, failure analysis, and corrective actions. Familiarity with supplier engagement, reliability testing at OSATs, and package process flows. Industry Knowledge: Familiarity with JEDEC, IPC, IEEE, and MIL-STD reliability standards. Soft Skills: Strong analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience in heterogeneous integration, fan-out packaging, chiplet architectures. Knowledge of electrical reliability mechanisms (e.g., electromigration, time-dependent dielectric breakdown). Expertise in AI-driven reliability modeling or machine learning for failure prediction. Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or related field (or equivalent practical experience). Strong knowledge of secondary mortgage processes and business event-to-accounting events flows. Experience partnering with cross-functional teams (Finance, Technology, Data) to deliver process and system enhancements. Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex requirements into clear documentation. Hands-on experience with requirements elicitation, process mapping, and documentation (e.g., user stories, acceptance criteria). Familiarity with relevant accounting standards (e.g., GAAP) and regulatory requirements. Experience with finance systems, ERP/accounting platforms, and/or business process automation. description_text: Job Posting Title: Executive Assistant, Programming Strategy (Disney Entertainment Television) Req ID: 10147850 Job Description: The Disney Entertainment Television Programming Strategy and Content Planning team is responsible for planning and implementing the programming strategy for all of Disney’s entertainment networks (ABC & ABC News, Nat Geo branded nets, FX branded nets, Freeform & Disney branded nets), related linear and non-linear platforms (TVE/VOD), Disney Branded and Nat Geo YouTube Channels, FAST channels, and all original content migration to Disney+ and Hulu. The Executive Assistant role sits at the heart of the Disney Entertainment Programming Strategy teams — supporting the daily magic behind Disney Branded Television, Freeform, FX and FAST content strategy. In this role, you’ll report to—and work side‑by‑side with—two VPs of Programming Strategy, helping them stay organized, informed, and ready for anything. The Executive Assistant (EA) manages both executive desks, inclusive of scheduling, expense processing, travel planning, and event coordination We’re looking for someone who brings exceptional organization, great people skills, and a knack for juggling lots of moving pieces with creativity and ease. In addition to two primary leaders, this individual serves as a team-wide resource, offering insight and support to the entire Programming Strategy group. This individual is also responsible for managing the collection and prompt distribution of weekly linear and multiplatform programming updates to key internal parties. In partnership with Research and other internal teams, the EA oversees recurring Competitive presentations, offering internal teams key industry insights. Additionally, the EA assists in implementing nonlinear content strategy for YouTube. This includes the creation of metadata, ordering, editing, and uploading short form video assets, screening content, creating thumbnails, and all other related duties. The EA updates internal databases and communicates all information / changes to key internal departments (i.e., Marketing, Publishing, Business Operations, Legal, etc.) and various external partners. If you love our Networks’ content and enjoy being the go‑to person who makes things happen, this role is for you. Responsibilities: Executive Administrative Support: Manage the administrative needs of two Executives. Schedule meetings and maintain calendars. Coordinate travel and process expense reports in Concur. Create and maintain distribution lists. Order office supplies through the Casual Buyer marketplace. Process monthly invoices from external vendors/consultants in SAP. Departmental Project & Presentation Support: Assist with departmental projects, including presentation development, reviewing internal materials, and research tasks. Create and update decks and documents in Keynote and PowerPoint. Gather presentation assets, including video and artwork assets, and organize files on Teams/SharePoint. Team Operations & Communications Support: Facilitate team communications, support in-person and virtual team events. Provide general on-site office support, including coordination with building staff for office moves, technology needs, and new hire setup etc. Content Tracking & Documentation: Update, maintain and distribute programming documents for Kids, FF, FX and FAST. Solicit and compile weekly linear and multiplatform performance updates across our channels and competitive networks. Compile and distribute monthly acquisition review materials. Data & Asset Management: Assist with metadata writing and program data entry across various databases. Organize project feedback and support database accuracy. Order and track delivery of video assets. Manage editing and uploading of content to YouTube channels. Design tailored thumbnails for channel optimization. Basic Qualifications: Strong passion for General Entertainment, with interest in Disney Networks content. 2+ years of Executive Assistant/Coordinator experience in a fast‑paced environment. Excellent organizational skills, including prioritization, time management, attention to detail, and process implementation. Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills. Self-starter with the ability to prioritize, meet deadlines, and pivot quickly. Detail-oriented, professional under pressure, and able to manage multiple projects at once. Proactive, resourceful, flexible, and able to anticipate needs. Flexibility to work across time zones and occasional overtime. Experience in a matrixed organization is a plus. We have an opening for an Emergency Management Specialist . You will be responsible for contributing to all-hazards emergency planning and preparedness programs in accordance with DOE and Laboratory requirements. You will help ensure emergency plans and procedures are integrated and executable, contribute to readiness and compliance activities, and coordinate across organizations to strengthen response capabilities and workforce protective action awareness. You will also support operational response activities as a member of the Emergency Response Organization. This position is in the Planning and Preparedness Division, Emergency Management Department. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. You will Develop, maintain, and update LLNL emergency plans, procedures, checklists, and Emergency Action Levels (EALs) for all-hazards incidents in alignment with DOE Order 151.1. Integrate technical analyses, including EPHA facility data, into emergency planning documents to ensure accurate hazard assessment and response strategies. Develop and refine Emergency Operations Center (EOC) processes for information management, decision support, and coordination with LLNL leadership and external agencies. Coordinate with Laboratory programs, facility management, and support organizations to ensure emergency plans are accurate, integrated, and executable. Ensure emergency planning activities comply with DOE/NNSA requirements, national emergency management standards, and applicable state and local partner expectations. Support the design and execution of emergency exercises and evaluate lessons learned from exercises, real incidents, and DOE events to strengthen response capabilities. Conduct programmatic assessments, readiness reviews, and documentation activities to identify gaps and demonstrate regulatory compliance. Serve as a member of the Emergency Response Organization, including qualification and participation in the Emergency Management Duty Officer (EMDO) off-hour duty rotation. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities, at the TSS.3 level Serve as a technical representative on formal and ad hoc teams addressing complex technical issues related to hazardous facility analysis; develop defensible, data-driven solutions. Perform computer modeling of hazardous material releases and consequence analyses to inform and scale emergency response capabilities. Develop technical reports and procedures and maintain Emergency Planning Hazards Assessments (EPHAs) for LLNL facilities with significant hazardous materials, applying rigorous hazards analysis methodologies. Develop and maintain Emergency Action Levels (EALs) to support rapid categorization and classification of Operational Emergencies. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Emergency Management or related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience in emergency management response and/or working in, or managing, an emergency management, site, or security operations center. Demonstrated ability to independently develop and implement moderately complex emergency management solutions using established DOE and Laboratory standards. Comprehensive working knowledge of DOE Order 151.1 and Emergency Action Level (EAL) development methodologies for Operational Emergency classification. Ability to analyze technical hazard information (e.g., EPHA data) and integrate findings into practical, executable emergency planning documentation. Proficiency in applying established emergency management principles to improve Emergency Operations Center (EOC) processes and decision-support frameworks. Demonstrated capability to coordinate across organizational boundaries to ensure alignment of emergency planning with programmatic, facility, and operational requirements. Working knowledge of national emergency management standards sufficient to support compliance documentation and readiness assessments. Ability to evaluate lessons learned from exercises and incidents and recommend process improvements within established policy frameworks. Proven capability to exercise sound independent judgment during emergency response operations, including participation in duty officer rotations and Emergency Response Organization activities. Additional qualifications at the TSS.3 level Advanced knowledge in hazardous facility analysis and demonstrated ability to independently analyze complex, not well-defined technical problems and develop defensible, data-driven solutions using sound judgment and creativity within established Laboratory and regulatory frameworks. Experience performing and interpreting computer modeling of hazardous material releases and consequence analyses; independently determining modeling approaches, evaluation criteria, and assumptions to support emergency preparedness and scalable response strategies. Proven ability to independently develop and maintain Emergency Planning Hazards Assessments (EPHAs), technical reports, and procedures for facilities with significant hazardous materials, applying advanced hazard analysis methodologies and exercising independent judgment in defining objectives and methods. Experience developing and maintaining Emergency Action Levels (EALs), applying advanced technical knowledge and independent judgment to ensure accurate categorization and classification of Operational Emergencies with programmatic and organizational impact. Working knowledge of DOE/NNSA regulatory requirements. Pay Range $129,150 - $163,764 Annually for the TSS.2 level $154,950 - $196,476 Annually for the TSS.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. Position Purpose: Provides day-to-day monitoring and basic plant and pump/booster station operations, routine lab tests and basic corrective and preventative maintenance activities. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Operates equipment manually and through instrumentation panels, computer terminals and programmable logic control units following process control procedures. Monitors and observes operating conditions, records observations and data in shift log. Diagnoses basic operational problems and takes corrective action per procedure. Performs routine CLAIR (cleaning, lubrication, adjustment, inspection and minor repair) on machines and related equipment which may include pumps, engines, centrifuges, generators, valves, gates, mixers, conveyors, blowers, dryers, chemical feed, odor control, disinfection equipment, vacuum filters and belt presses. Reports and documents results of work performed and enters into appropriate database. Promptly reports any operational problems with machines or equipment to Lead or Supervisor. Collects water, wastewater, industrial waste, groundwater, sludge, residuals and/or gas samples according to schedule. Performs field tests (chemical, physical and biological) in order to pace chemical dosages for process and odor control units. Prepares chemical solutions, monitors supplies and recommends reorder. Performs routine lab tests and prepares reports per procedure. Performs routine instrument calibration for portable meters including, but not limited to, dissolved oxygen, pH, H2S, percent oxygen, lower explosive limit. Learns to inspect and becomes proficient at mechanical troubleshooting to determine repairs needed. Dismantles equipment to gain access to and repairs defective parts using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing devices. Re-assembles and tests equipment ensuring safe and efficient operating condition is restored. Learns to troubleshoot hydraulic, pneumatic and electronic equipment and instrumentation. Performs manual labor including cleaning equipment, facilities and grounds as required and properly disposes of waste according to safety and environmental policies. Operates vehicles, mobile equipment and material handling equipment for operational and maintenance purposes. Performs facility maintenance and repair and may replace or install light bulbs, fluorescent tubes, damaged glass, windows, doors, partitions, ceiling or floor tiles, door locks, carpet, and/or paint. Learns to estimate time and material costs for various projects. May assist in other areas of facility as directed. Work Environment: Spends 100% of the time in operations environment. Typically spends 25 – 35% of time exposed to outdoor and sometimes inclement weather. Company service vehicles are used as required. Travels 1 – 2 times per year for company provided training. May be required to travel up to five consecutive days. May serve rotational 24 hour emergency on-call. Possible Work Hazards : May be exposed to possible operations hazards including fumes, dust, toxic and caustic chemicals, noise, rotating machinery, high pressure and hot and cold temperatures, slippery surfaces, water and electrical hazards. Education/Experience/Background: High school or GED with the ability to read, write and comprehend English (operational, process, safety and quality instructions) and be able to carry out verbal and written instructions. Six months to two years of experience in a related position with experience in a similar environment preferred with ability to comprehend specifications, blueprints and manuals. Experience using material handling equipment, pressure gauges and precision measuring instruments. Experience using power, pneumatic, hydraulic and hand tools and shop tools such as drill press, band saw, bench grinder, torque wrench preferred. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations. Some vocational training and mechanical aptitude preferred, with the ability to read, interpret and record data from meters, gauges, scales, panels, computer consoles and other equipment. Must have the ability to diagnose basic and routine process and mechanical problems and take remedial corrective action. Must have basic computer skills and have ability to operate programs for process control, the Computer Maintenance Management System, and laboratory/industrial pretreatment QA/QC. Must consistently demonstrate the ability to learn and independently perform assigned duties and meet or exceed production and quality goals. Must demonstrate ability to work in a team environment and willingness to assume additional or new responsibilities readily. Must be able to serve rotational 24-hour emergency on-call if required by site. Required Certification/Licenses/Training: Minimum water/wastewater license as required by regulatory agency at site. Must possess a valid driver’s license and a safe driving record. Employee Orientation, Departmental Operating Procedures, Safety, OSHA and Quality Training. HAZWOPER (Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response) Level I and II First Responder Certification if required by site. Obtain and maintain minimum water / wastewater operator state certification. Must become proficient in the care and use of all site specific, facility required PPE (Personal Protection Equipment), including respirators, gas detectors, confined space equipment, etc.) Forklift Certification if required by site. Training in operation of mechanical drives, hydraulic pumps and valves, pneumatics, electronics and control systems. Obtain HVAC, Electrician, Plumber’s or other trade License if assigned to that area. Note : Tech will not perform duties unless properly licensed. Training in the use of energy management systems as needed. Works toward increasing skills in additional functional areas or in obtaining advanced skills / maintenance certifications. May perform more advanced functions as part of training and development. Physical Requirements: Amount of time spent – Standing 25%, Walking 75% for as many as five miles per shift. Requires close visual and hearing observation to detect non-conformance and machine malfunction. Constantly uses hands to finger, handle or feel and frequently reaches with hands and arms. Works in various positions; works on ladders, catwalks, and supports at heights of 50 feet above the ground; and works with hands extended above and below head and body up to 40 minutes using hand tools weighing up to 15 pounds. Must be able to lift and carry 50 pounds (occasionally 60 pounds) distances of 10 feet. Occasional stooping, bending or kneeling and entering confined spaces.

AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in the Southwest or Western part of the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Position Purpose: Performs a variety of semi-skilled, skilled, technical, and administrative work in the planning, scheduling, maintenance of vehicles and equipment within Fleet Services. Replacement of hand tools due to damage or breakage in the normal performance of the job will be reimbursed after approval by the Plant Manager. Employee Orientation, Departmental Operating Procedures, OSHA and Quality Training. Veolia equipment training. Obtain and continue ASE certification in Master Automotive Technician or Master Medium / Heavy Duty Truck Technician within three years from date of hire. HAZWOPER (Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response) Level I and II First Responder Certification. Work toward higher level water / wastewater treatment certification. Forklift Certification if required by site. Physical Requirements: Amount of time spent – Standing 75%, Walking 25%. Requires close visual and hearing observation to detect non-conformance and equipment malfunction. Constantly uses hands to finger, handle or feel and frequently reaches with hands and arms. Works in various positions; works on ladders, and works with hands extended above and below head and body up to 40 minutes using hand and power tools weighing up to 15 pounds. Must be able to lift and carry 50 pounds (occasionally 60 pounds) distances of 10 feet. Occasional stooping, bending or kneeling and entering confined spaces.

The Associate Director provides statistical programming support for multiple clinical projects across multiple therapeutic areas, both through individual contribution and through the work of staff. The Associate Director provides training and performance management for staff. The Associate Director demonstrates leadership competencies, builds relationships, and promotes teamwork within the Statistical Programming organization and across functions. The Associate Director is accountable for ensuring statistical programming support is delivered across multiple therapeutic areas. The Associate Director makes key recommendations and decisions related to processes, standards, and resource management. The Associate Director is also responsible for staff management and development. Responsibilities: SAS Programming: Demonstrates a strong understanding of SAS programming concepts and techniques used in the pharmaceutical industry and applies that knowledge to resolve non-routine problems. Standards: Oversees the development and implementation of global company standards for output design and programming conventions and monitors regulatory guidance and industry best practices. CRFs and Database Definitions: Provides strategic guidance on CRF and database design and reviews global standards related to these deliverables. Derivation Programming, Submission Data Sets, and Programs: Interprets statistical analysis plans, develops analysis data set specifications, and oversees the development and implementation of global standards for derived data sets and submission programs. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Works collaboratively with stakeholders to manage priorities and resources across therapeutic areas. Demonstrates a solid understanding of drug development principles, anticipates risks, develops contingency and escalation plans, and contributes to cross-functional initiatives. Communication: Presents statistical programming concepts, risk assessments, and recommendations clearly and persuasively to statisticians, scientists, programmers, and non-scientists. Effectively leads meetings and presentations. Training and Mentoring: Provides guidance, training, and mentoring to staff to support development and ensure compliance with training requirements. Staff Management : Assigns responsibilities, defines scope, and reviews progress to ensure projects are delivered on time and with appropriate quality. Allocates resources to maintain the right balance of expertise across projects and collaborates with management to assess staffing needs. Sets high expectations, promotes open communication, and leads staff to meet organizational goals. Provides performance management for 4–10 statistical programmers. Minimum Qualifications: Degree in Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field 10+ years of statistical programming experience (with MS) OR 12+ years of statistical programming experience (with BS) Strong technical competence in SAS programming and macro development. Experience in pharmaceutical clinical trials. Experience with regulatory filings such as NDA, BLA, or other submissions, including ISS and ISE experience. Preferred Qualifications: Experience interacting with regulatory agencies, especially FDA and EMEA. Previous management experience. Other Required Skills: Working knowledge of ICH guidelines and relevant regulatory requirements. Strong oral and written communication skills.

Bachelor's Degree in related field or 1-2 years of experience in Materials Management or Operations; 1-2 years of experience in Purchasing/Maintenance or 2 minimum total combined years of experience. SAP experience strongly preferred.

The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

The Mastering Coordinator supports NBCUniversal’s Studio Mastering organization by coordinating mastering and sub-mastering workflows that enable timely, accurate delivery of content across the company’s distribution supply chain. This role translates customer and distribution requirements into executable mastering workflows, identifies appropriate source materials, and partners with internal teams, StudioPost Operations, and external vendors to ensure work is delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with Studio Mastering technical specifications. Define mastering and sub-mastering approaches based on specifications, delivery formats, timelines, and budget constraints. Serve as a day-to-day point of coordination for assigned mastering work, escalating risks and issues as needed. Prime contact for editorial workflow support, assisting editors and workflow specific to editorial projects and servicing Cross-Functional & Vendor Coordination Partner with StudioPost Operations Project Managers to ensure work is completed on schedule and within approved budgets. Coordinate with third-party service providers to support mastering and sub-mastering execution. Maintain ongoing communication with Studio Mastering leadership regarding job status, priorities, and technical considerations. Asset Research & Source Element Identification Research inventory systems and historical records to determine the most appropriate source elements for each mastering request. Collaborate with Studio Mastering subject-matter experts to leverage knowledge of asset history, specifications, and condition. Tracking, Reporting & Continuous Improvement Track and report job-level metrics, including status, work completed, remaining scope, and cost-to-date. Contribute to ongoing evaluation and improvement of mastering specifications, workflows, and operational processes. Stay current with evolving mastering standards, delivery specifications, and industry trends. Basic Requirements: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in motion picture or television post-production. 3+ years of experience in film, video, and/or audio post-production environments. Solid understanding of physical and file-based mastering workflows. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Desired Characteristics: Experience utilizing Smartsheets and Dolby version Experience supporting studio-level mastering or distribution operations. Understanding of feature film and television production and post-production lifecycles. Ability to identify workflow efficiencies and support best-practice implementation. Strong customer service mindset and collaborative communication style. We have an opening for a Cloud Operations Engineer to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing cloud solutions that support the National Nuclear Security Administration’s (NNSA) business services and programmatic missions, including scientific research and mission-critical operations. This position is in the Enterprise Infrastructure Services (EIS) Division within the Computing Directorate. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to drive innovation, improve scalability, and ensure the secure and efficient utilization of cloud resources for NNSA initiatives. This role supports multiple sites across the country and occasional travel is required to collaborate with stakeholders and partners. This position offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and highly technical environment, supporting critical infrastructure for enterprise-level applications. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either the SES.2 or SES.3 level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Deploy and manage cloud infrastructure (primarily AWS) in support of scientific, engineering, and business applications. Develop automation scripts and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions for cloud resource provisioning and management. Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and IT staff to migrate workloads and optimize applications for cloud environments. Implement and manage cloud financial operations (FinOps) practices to optimize cloud spending, track usage, and collaborate with stakeholders to ensure cost-effective resource allocation. Monitor cloud performance and usage, and implement solutions for high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. Ensure compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) and NNSA security policies and federal regulations for cloud operations. Provide technical support, documentation, and training for cloud users across the enterprise. Stay abreast of emerging cloud technologies and recommend adoption of innovative solutions. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the SES.3 Level Develop and implement advanced cloud computing environments that align with customer needs and enterprise system strategies, ensuring optimal performance and scalability. Independently configure and utilize systems and cloud management tools to monitor, maintain, and optimize infrastructure operations effectively. Identify, troubleshoot, and document complex system and network issues to ensure timely resolution and minimize disruptions. Ability to obtain and maintain a US DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. Citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of technical education and relevant experience. Broad experience in cloud platform administration and support, with proficiency in technologies such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or hybrid cloud environments. Broad knowledge of cloud infrastructure operations, including resource provisioning, automation, and the use of infrastructure management tools. Proficient understanding of cloud support systems, such as virtual networking, identity and access management, and monitoring solutions. Comprehensive experience with cloud architecture documentation tools, including Visio and other office productivity software. Proficient in managing and troubleshooting cloud-based resources and services, including performance monitoring and incident response. Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with customers and team members. Additional Qualifications at the SES.3 Level Significant experience managing enterprise cloud environments, including platforms such as AWS, Azure, and hybrid cloud networking. Advanced knowledge of troubleshooting techniques, with strong skills in resolving issues through analysis of logs, metrics, and cloud-native diagnostic tools. Significant experience with resource provisioning, automation, and infrastructure as management tools, such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Cloud Development Kit, or similar platforms. Significant experience training and mentoring team members, focusing on cloud engineering best practices and architectural design principles. Desired Qualifications Active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top-Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire. AWS Certified Solutions Architect credential or an equivalent advanced cloud certification. Deep familiarity with hybrid cloud architectures and expert-level proficiency in integrating on-premises environments with cloud platforms in air-gapped environments. Comprehensive knowledge of compliance frameworks, such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), FedRAMP, and related standards, with proven experience implementing and maintaining compliance within cloud environments.
